guidelines.description: The framework for the development of the cultural register is formed by four cultural policy guidelines on which the KRB has agreed with the Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion:
items: Evidence-based cultural policy and cultural urban development: The Berlin cultural cadastre creates a comprehensive data base about cultural areas in order to enable fact-based cultural policy and targeted urban development.
Securing and redeveloping spaces for culture: The cultural cadastre serves as an instrument for sustainable monitoring of cultural areas in order to support their preservation and open up new spaces.

Fair distribution of cultural offerings in the urban space and equal opportunities with regard to participation: The cultural register visualizes gaps in cultural offerings and supports city planning in creating a balanced and fair cultural offering for all Berliners.

Improving collaboration between departments, levels and sectors: As a flexible digital planning tool, the cultural cadastre strengthens collaboration within the various areas of responsibility, administrative levels and the entire Berlin cultural scene.

introduction: In a growing metropolis like Berlin, art and cultural spaces are scarce resources.
The cultural register is mentioned in the government policy guidelines for this legislative period.

barriers.description: The cultural locations in the cultural cadastre are currently only displayed via an interactive map view.

barriers.description: Some interactive elements of the website - in particular filter functions, map elements or navigation points - cannot currently be operated via keyboard.
barriers.measures: The technical structure of the website is being revised to ensure full keyboard control of all interactive elements.
barriers.timeline: Implementation will take place by the end of 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Keyboard operability

barriers.description: When navigating with the keyboard, the visible focus is not clearly visible on all interactive elements.
barriers.measures: The visual focus design is overhauled so that interactive elements are clearly highlighted as you scroll through.
barriers.timeline: Implementation will take place by the end of 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Visible focus

barriers.description: Some icons or buttons on the website do not have meaningful alternative text.
barriers.measures: All graphic elements are checked and provided with correct alternative texts.
barriers.title: Barrier: Alternative texts for images and symbols

barriers.description: The semantic structure of the website is not fully defined by ARIA roles and landmarks.
barriers.measures: The page structure is supplemented with semantic HTML elements and ARIA roles to improve orientation for assistive technologies.
barriers.timeline: Implementation will take place by the end of 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Missing ARIA roles and landmarks

barriers.description: The hierarchical structure of the headings is not implemented correctly on all pages.
barriers.measures: The HTML structure is revised to ensure a consistent and logical heading structure.
barriers.timeline: The correction will take place during 2026.
barriers.title: Barrier: Unstructured headings (h1–h6)

barriers.measures: The interactions are technically checked and supplemented to provide feedback to screen readers.
barriers.title: Barrier: Lack of feedback during interactions

introduction: Since September 2025, the Berlin Cultural Cadastre, the first version of our digital tool that systematically records Berlin's cultural landscape, has been available to you.

The cultural cadastre continues to grow: Version 2 is planned for the beginning of 2026, and version 3 will follow in mid-2026. With each new version, we include more cultural locations, supplement the information and add new functionalities.
You can help us with this.
The current version of the cultural register is version 1.
